ACADEMIC RESEARCH

Faculty-Sponsored Graduate Research: University of Texas at Austin
Summer 2020 to Present with Dr. Thibaud Taillefumier - Department of Neuroscience

  • Designed entirely novel mathematical and computational analysis of neural activity that culminated in a first-author publication in PRX, the most prestigious journal in physics (Becker et al. 2024).
  • Expanded the scope of analysis to heterogeneous model of neural activity by leveraging rigorous techniques from queueing theory, currently reviewed in PLoS Comp. Bio (Becker et al. 2025).
  • Analyzed neural data collected in behaving mammals through the lens of the theoretical tools mentioned above.

Technical Associate 1: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Florida Atlantic University
March 2019 - July 2019 and January 2020 - June 2020 with Dr. Carmen Varela at Picower Institute for Learning and Memory at MIT

  • Led a first author study analyzing time-series data to quantify the effects of pharmacological agents on different frequency bands of measured signals and their effects on phase amplitude coupling (Becker et al. 2020).
  • Managed startup of new neuroscience laboratory at Florida Atlantic University with responsibilities including training new students and building lab hardware.

Faculty-Sponsored Graduate Research: Stony Brook University
Summer 2017 to Fall 2019 with Dr. Memming Park - Department of Neurobiology and Behavior

  • Led a study to develop a biophysically inspired novel neuronal model to predict observed spike times.
  • Model-fit high-dimensional neural data using stochastic gradient descent methods.

Faculty-Sponsored Undergraduate Research: Stony Brook University
Fall 2016 - Spring 2017 with Dr. Memming Park - Department of Neurobiology and Behavior

  • Examined properties of coupled oscillating systems within neurons through signal processing techniques.

DATA SCIENCE PROJECTS

  • Time Series Analysis/Signal Processing (MATLAB): Utilized Fourier/spectral analysis on cortical activity to quantify changes in time-dependent high-frequency activity in response to sleep-aid medications (Becker et al. 2020).
  • Machine Learning/Neural Networks (Python): Developed a stepwise learning approach using PyTorch to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in image classification tasks, improving model generalization on novel classes.
  • Predictive Models/Machine Learning (Python): Created and trained a flexible biophysically inspired model using stochastic machine learning algorithms (ADAM) to predict both over- and underdispersed discrete spiking events.

PROFESSIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS

  • Chateaubriand Fellow: Prestigious award from the French Foreign Affairs Ministry that fully funded a 6-month independent research project at Université de Paris, France titled “Emergence and Self-consistency of Spike Correlations in Recurrent Neural Networks”.
  • Mentoring: Developed computational training for graduate students with support from the National Science Foundation.
  • Science Communication: Presented research at national and international conferences (Society for Neuroscience, Computational System Neuroscience, Gulf Coast Consortium, International conference for mathematical neuroscience).
